title: Legal entity, establishment, tax, regulator and client-money scopes are orthogonal
summary: Accounting Core treats establishment/place of business, tax registration, tax election, regulatory registration, client-money arrangement and reporting boundary as independent relationships of a legal entity. These scopes annotate and select one entity's economic books; they do not redefine the entity.
invariants: A legal entity can have several establishments and several tax/regulatory registrations without becoming several accounting companies.
A foreign tax registration does not imply a local establishment or local subsidiary.
A client-money arrangement associates exact establishment/regulator/currency context but does not encode regulator-specific safeguarding rules.
Journal line dimensions preserve exact scope identities so historical reporting does not depend only on mutable current registries.
A ReportingBoundary selects existing immutable lines; it does not copy, rewrite or repost them.
Currency remains part of aggregation identity so multi-currency reports do not add incompatible monetary units.

provenance.claim: Legal entity, establishment, tax registration/election, regulatory registration, client money and reporting boundaries are independent concepts.
